answer: DeepWalk (Perozzi et al., 2014) generates truncated random walks over the graph and feeds them to the Skip-gram model with hierarchical softmax (word2vec), treating each walk as a sentence. Skip-gram with negative sampling is implicitly factorizing a matrix whose entries are shifted pointwise mutual information values of node co-occurrences within a fixed window in the random walks (Levy & Goldberg, 2014; Qiu et al., 2018 showed DeepWalk approximates factorizing a matrix of the form (1/T) sum_{r=1}^{T} (D^{-1}A)^r D^{-1} minus a log(b) shift). Because random walks of limited length tend to stay within densely connected regions, nodes in the same community co-occur frequently in walks, so their co-occurrence statistics (the proximity matrix) are similar. The low-rank factorization then forces these nodes to receive similar embedding vectors, so community structure is preserved. In short, it is the random-walk-based high-order proximity (multi-step transition probabilities that favor intra-community paths) captured by the implicit low-rank factorization that preserves communities. Note that the original DeepWalk paper does not explicitly perform a matrix factorization; the factorization view is an analysis of the Skip-gram objective.
